notes:
Parts and best parts, for every clip
- Every clip is now split into parts, and Cut Valet picks its best parts in two lanes: best sound (a thought someone finished saying, even across short pauses) and best picture (a clean stretch with something happening). The clip inspector shows them on a bar you can split, merge and nudge, and your edits stick.
- Media tiles say how many best parts a clip has, and hovering starts on the best one.
- Selects can take up to three best parts per clip, and the AI assistant sees parts when it plans an edit.
- Footage analysed before this update can be measured for parts from a one-time offer per project.

Bringing footage in
- New Project pointed at a folder that already has photos or videos in it now offers to bring them in, right where they are, and starts their tools.
- Project > Rescan for New Clips now also finds photos and videos in the project's folders that were never imported, brings them in, and queues only what they still need.
- Dragging in files that already live inside the project leaves them where they are by default. The choice is now two clear buttons: Copy into the project, or Leave them where they are.
- After bringing a folder in where it is, Cut Valet offers once to watch it, so new files you add there come in by themselves.
- A card left with an old shoot on it no longer gets copied again into a new project: clips already in another project are skipped (Copy anyway brings them in).
- Photos dropped in now get their analysis queued, like videos always did.
- A new switch, Analyse photos (Settings > Analysis), skips analysis for stills when you only shot a few. Timelapses still count as footage.
- Photos can be kept out of Resolve entirely (Send photos to Resolve, Settings > Resolve).
- Project locations remember the drive, not just its letter, and a different drive with the same name is refused.
- A card the project drive cannot hold is refused before the copy, and a copy that fills the drive stops cleanly.
- A card with clips from two cameras files each clip under its own camera.

Resolve
- Photos land in a Photography bin, matching the folders on disk.
- New per-project option: Bins follow my folders. Files that stay where they are go into bins named after their folders (New Project, or right-click a project > Resolve bins).
- Time-of-day timelines no longer stack lanes or rebuild over and over while a card copies, and Resync repairs one that went wrong.
- Let Resolve rest between syncs (Settings > Resolve, off by default): closes the idle Cut Valet project to free memory and reopens it for the next sync. It leaves the project open while you are working in it.

Your AI agent (MCP)
- Cut Valet can run with no window (--dvea-headless) so an agent can create projects and work in the library while the app is closed. Opening the app takes over cleanly.
- ingest_files skips files another project already holds (copy_anyway overrides) and takes a project_id.

Speed and reliability
- Signals runs before previews when they compete, gets more decoding threads, and decodes HEVC on an NVIDIA card when there is room.
- Many short freezes are gone: the Projects page, the project switcher, the backup chip and the activity log no longer wait on the database while an ingest writes.
- A database write that was interrupted can no longer leave the library locked until you quit.
- Analysis sidecars back up once their clip's analysis settles, instead of after every pass.
- On a Mac, Cut Valet asks macOS not to nap it while it is working.
- Sony HIF photos get their on-screen text read.
- A local AI model that crashes mid-answer is caught and paused, instead of its half answer being used.
